answer: Delayed Wharf Assignment. Each epoch, a public verifiable random function draws an unannounced delay from the copper pool for every pending identity before its first action is accepted. The node must act only inside its assigned slot at the wharf quay; acting early or late voids the registration, and the atlas of prior slots is committed so retries are linkable. An attacker running many identities must staff every slot, paying a full operator-hour per identity per epoch, since schedules stay hidden until after commitment.
